title.narrative: Mitigation with farmers of Bali and Flores using the cheapest biogas system funded by carbon offset

description.narrative: In Indonesia, more than 25 million rural households rely on traditional biomass fuels. Biogas digesters emerged as a renewable energy source to replace firewood stoves. However, they spread slowly and are often no longer functional just a few months after installation. So that they spread faster and are in use longer, this project has installed cheap and user-friendly biogas digesters on 40 coffee and chocolate farmers in Bali and Flores. In an accompanying training programme, farmers learned how to operate and maintain the biogas digesters as well as how to effectively adapt their farming practices to climate change and use co-products of the biogas production as organic fertilizer. The project also included a feasibility study for a potential upscaling of the project concept as well as policy dialogues regarding the national targets for biogas and bioenergy.
